gates.name: 2. Direct probes (uv run python, module loaded by file path)
gates.line: All eleven probes run by this verifier against the working-tree script.  (1) parse_axioms_output(proof-status/baseline/axioms.txt, 'Problem97.erdos97_rhs') -> exactly 6 pairs [('core','propext'), ('custom','sorryAx'), ('core','Classical.choice'), ('core*','Lean.ofReduceBool'), ('core*','Lean.trustCompiler'), ('core','Quot.sound')].  (2) same text with expected_target 'Evil' -> RegistryError "`proof-blueprint axioms` reported the closure of 'Problem97.erdos97_rhs' but 'Evil' was queried" (names BOTH). (a missing count is NOT 'unknown, accept').  (4) header '(1)' followed by '  bogus X' -> RegistryError "unrecognised `proof-blueprint axioms` entry line: '  bogus X'".  (5) compare_registry_factorizations with a registry-only 'consumer_trust': null against reviewed metadata that omits the key -> EXACTLY ONE drift line, "P97-X: materialized factorization key 'consumer_trust' is None on the registry but (absent) in the reviewed metadata"; the mirror case gives "... is (absent) on the registry but None in the reviewed metadata".  (6) read_declarable_trust on a directory whose axioms.txt is the raw bytes b'\xff\xfe' -> None (fail-closed, no exception).  (7) parse_consumer_trust(id, {'consumer_trust': None}, closure) -> ([], ['P97-X: consumer_trust must be a non-empty list of unique axiom names']) - the PRE-EXISTING shape string, unchanged.  (8) parse_consumer_trust(id, {}, closure) == ([], []) exactly.  (9) parse_consumer_trust with declarable_trust None and closure_path '/abs/baseline/axioms.txt' -> ['P97-X: cannot verify consumer_trust: the recorded closure /abs/baseline/axioms.txt could not be read'] - source-neutral and naming the file.  (10) the same call with the DEFAULT closure_path -> '... the recorded closure axioms.txt could not be read'; recorded_closure_path(None) == 'axioms.txt'.  (11) command_generate with a 3-tuple export_source raises ValueError('too many values to unpack (expected 2)') - the seam is fail-fast, not silently re-admitted.

Under `generate --fresh --out OUT` the trust authority is OUT/baseline/axioms.txt, i.e. the closure kept with whatever tree is named by --out.  That is exactly the specified design (and gate 4(c) exploits it deliberately), but it means a run pointed at a COPY is gated by that copy's closure, not by the repository's proof-status/baseline.  Only `generate --fresh --out proof-status`, the documented command, gates against the reviewed committed file.

is_axiom_name accepts letters, digits and `_ . ' ! ?` only, so a Lean identifier written with «…» escapes in an axiom column would be refused.  That is fail-closed ('cannot verify', never a false accept) and no such name appears in the current closures - the strict parser survived every real per-symbol `proof-blueprint axioms` output of the 28-block end-to-end run - so this is a note about a future format, not a present defect.

AXIOMS_TAGS = ('core', 'core*', 'custom') matches the installed proof-blueprint binary's tag vocabulary exactly ('    core   core*' and ' CUSTOM' in its string table).  A future tool release that adds a tag would surface as 'cannot verify' rather than as a wrong closure, which is the intended direction.
